compiled_state.title: As an orchestrator, leaked commits with DSO-Bug trailers are detected and routed to the correct sub-branch after each fix-bug, after each batch, and at Phase K
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Run `detect-session-leakage.sh` inline (a) after each fix-bug invocation in Bug-Fix Mode, (b) after each batch completion in Phase F/G, (c) once at Phase K as a safety-net final sweep. Handle the closed-bug-trailer race specifically.

**Why**: Earlier-and-more-frequent leak detection keeps the session worktree clean and surfaces misrouted commits while the current-sub-branch context is still warm.

**Scope**:
- IN: Three invocation points: post-fix-bug (Bug-Fix Mode), post-batch (Phase F/G), Phase K final sweep; invocations use `STORY_BRANCH_PREFIX=bug-batch/` (env var from S1) and resolve current sub-branch from S7's `DEBUG_BRANCH_TRACKING:` anchor; closed-bug-trailer race protection: when a sub-agent commit's `DSO-Bug:` trailer references a ticket already closed during parallel batch execution, log SHA + closed-ticket-id and route to `--force-route-to-pending` state rather than stalling.
- OUT: Parameterizing `detect-session-leakage.sh` itself (S1); the 5-case matrix logic (existing infrastructure).

## Done Definitions

- When complete, `detect-session-leakage.sh` runs after every fix-bug invocation in Bug-Fix Mode with `STORY_BRANCH_PREFIX=bug-batch/` and routes any leaked `DSO-Bug:`-trailed commits to the matching sub-branch
  ← Satisfies: "After each fix-bug invocation, detect-session-leakage.sh runs"
- When complete, `detect-session-leakage.sh` runs after every Phase F/G batch completion and after the Phase K final sweep with the same routing
  ← Satisfies: "After each batch completion in Phase F/G, detect-session-leakage.sh runs; final end-of-session sweep at Phase K"
- When complete, a sub-agent commit referencing a ticket closed during parallel batch execution does not stall integration — its SHA + closed-ticket-id is logged and the commit is routed to `--force-route-to-pending` state
  ← Satisfies: "Closed-bug-trailer race protection"
- When complete, leak detection inline overhead is sub-second per invocation under normal session load (verified by timing harness)
  ← Satisfies: "Inline leak detection cadence"
- Unit tests written and passing for closed-bug-trailer race + each invocation point
  ← Satisfies: "Leak detection invocation cadence"

## Considerations

- [Performance] Per-invocation overhead must be sub-second; timing harness in tests asserts the bound
- [Reliability] Closed-bug-trailer race protection is a derived requirement from the red-team review — explicit test required

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
